title: UDLF deployment config — SentinelOne STAR Rules
description: Optional, opt-in sub-schema for the `config` block of a UDLF deployment whose `platform` is `sentinel-one`. Covers SentinelOne STAR rules. This is not a scheduled-search platform: STAR rules evaluate continuously, so there is no schedule block, and a rule may carry active-response actions that quarantine an endpoint. The fields UDLF already owns are absent — maturity and runtime behaviour come from `lifecycle` and `mode`, authorship from `metadata.authors`, and each target tenant is its own deployment entry — as are vendor-assigned rule ids, because UDLF is desired-state only. For a `Single Event` rule the S1QL query lives in `detection_content` like any other language. For a `Correlation` rule the subqueries stay here, because they are structural parts of the rule definition rather than one logic blob — the one place logic legitimately leaks into `config`, pending the correlation-primitive decision in the v0.3.0 roadmap. This schema is NOT referenced by the UDLF core schema; apply it separately when you want the block validated.

then.$comment: A Single Event rule matches one query with no correlation; its S1QL comes from detection_content.
A Correlation rule is defined entirely by its correlation block.

Active response actions operate on a process, so SentinelOne only permits them on Single Event rules or correlations grouped by the Process entity. The inverse (response is required in those two cases) is left to the deployer, since a partially-authored UDLF config is legitimate.

schema.description: Self-identifying sub-schema version for this config block, so this file can version independently of UDLF core.

details.description: Optional overrides for how the rule presents in SentinelOne. Omit any field to let the deployer take it from the detection.

name.description: Rule name. Overrides the detection title for this deployment.

description.description: Rule description. Overrides `detection_context.description` for this deployment.

severity.description: Severity the rule raises with. Overrides `detection_context.severity` for this deployment.

expiration.description: Expiry date as YYYY-MM-DD, at most six months out from deployment. Rules are Permanent until this is set, at which point SentinelOne treats them as Temporary. Useful for time-boxed campaign or incident rules.

condition.description: What the rule matches on. Note that SentinelOne cannot change a rule's condition type after deployment — switching means deleting the rule and deploying a new one, which also means clearing any deployer-held rule id.

type.description: `Single Event` alerts on each match of a single query, whose S1QL lives in `detection_content`. `Correlation` groups multiple subqueries around a shared entity over a time window, defined in `correlation` below.

correlation.description: Correlation rule definition. Required when `type` is `Correlation`.

entity.description: Entity that groups matching events. Each maps to a fixed field set: Process = agent.uuid AND src.process.uid; User = any of actor.user.name, src/tgt.process.user, event.login.userName; Ip = any of src/dst endpoint and process ip fields; Endpoint = agent.uuid OR device.uid; Storyline = src.process.storyline.id AND agent.uuid. Only `Process` permits active response actions.

match_in_order.description: Require the subqueries to match in the order listed. Set false to match them in any order within the window.

time_window.description: Window within which all subqueries must match. SentinelOne accepts only these fixed values.

sub_queries.description: Ordered subqueries making up the correlation. These are rule structure rather than a single logic blob, which is why they live here rather than in `detection_content`.

query.description: Subquery in S1QL 2.0. Version 1.0 is not supported.

matches_required.description: How many times this subquery must match within the window.

cool_off.description: Suppress repeat alerts for this period after the rule fires, from 1m to 1440m or 1h to 24h. Note that mitigation actions set in `response` are NOT applied to suppressed alerts — a long cool-off silently disables response for the duration.

response.description: Storyline Active Response actions taken when the rule matches. Permitted only on Single Event rules and Process-entity correlations. These actions change endpoint state, so a deployment carrying them is doing more than detecting — consider whether the UDLF deployment `mode` still reflects reality.

treat_as_threat.description: Promote the alert to a threat and apply the matching threat policy. `false` leaves it as an alert; `Suspicious` and `Malicious` select the respective policy.

network_quarantine.description: Automatically network-quarantine the alerting endpoint. Reconnection is manual, from the Sentinels page or Endpoint Details.

advanced.description: Escape hatch for SentinelOne API properties this sub-schema does not model. Passed through verbatim, so keys must match the API exactly. Prefer a modelled field where one exists — anything here is unvalidated and invisible to tooling.
